dedupe_keys.name: epri dcflex retail flexible load tariff sample dataset and data centre operator survey

description: DCFlex is an initiative launched by the Electric Power Research Institute in October 2024 with more than 65 utilities, grid operators, regulators, hyperscale cloud companies and technology firms, including Google, Meta, Oracle, Microsoft and NVIDIA, to show how data centres can vary their electricity use to support the grid and connect faster. Its programmes workstream publishes public deliverables that include a Retail Flexible Load Tariff Sample Dataset, released in August 2025, which compiles 159 retail tariffs from 71 US electric utilities that offer interruptible, demand response and standby, backup or cogeneration rates and programmes for large loads, and a global survey of data centre owners and operators, released in August 2026, analysing 1,126 responses from twelve countries on their willingness and ability to offer flexibility. Other deliverables cover retail programmes and wholesale markets, the PJM market response to large load growth, community acceptance and Texas Senate Bill 6. The initiative also runs nine demonstration sites and is developing the Flex MOSAIC framework to describe flexibility by magnitude, timing, duration and frequency. Coverage: United States utilities for the tariffs; twelve countries for the survey. Format and access: EPRI product downloads, free public deliverables; formats not stated. Caveats: the tariff list is a sample, not a census; survey answers are self-reported. Simulation uses: demand response and backup generation parameters for data centres in power system models, and interdependency studies of large loads and grids. Related records: the IM3 and EPRI load projections and the NLR workload power profiles give demand shapes.
